newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firm as year-end balance-squaring nears.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firm as year-end balance-squaring nears.

text.p: The rouble was little changed in active trading on Tuesday, but dealers said rouble demand was steady as banks actively sought funds before closing year-end balance sheets.
roubles/dollar Dec 10 midday Dec 10 early Dec 9 close
"The situation is standard for year-end. Rouble fever is starting as banks need roubles to close their balances," United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov said.
Rouble demand is likely to dominate the market until the market returns in early 1997 to its usual state, and the rouble resumes its slow decline in line with central bank policy, he said.
An Interbank Finance House dealer said trading was lively despite narrow spreads, with rates fluctuating both ways.
Another dealer said Wednesday's government bond auctions might be another source of rouble support.
On December 11, the central bank is auctioning 8.5 trillion roubles of GKO Treasury bills and three trillion roubles of OFZ bonds.
